samples.summary: The newly hardened self-review bound is still bypassable with `--round N`, the same shape of bypass the delta just closed for `--fresh`
samples.evidence: This delta turned the round bound into a hard refusal and closed the `--fresh` bypass by measuring `spentRound` against `nextRound(onDiskBefore)` (line 974). The sibling override is left open: at line 966 an explicit `--round` wins unconditionally (`round = Number(args.round)`), and `spentRound` only consults the pre-delete rounds when `args.fresh` is set. So with MAX rounds already on disk, `node scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs review --round 1` gives `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`, the refusal at line 976 never fires, no `--force` notice is printed, `prior = round > 1 ? … : []` (line 1026) carries NOTHING forward, and `mkdirSync(dir)` (line 1012) overwrites round-1's verdicts — which are exactly the verdicts a later round would have read back. That is verbatim the failure the new comment at lines 967-973 describes ("exactly how a fourth round presents itself as a clean first one … silently loses its carry-forward on the way past a gate"), reachable through the flag the delta did not touch. `--round` legitimately exists to RETRY a number after a 429, so the consistent fix is to measure the bound on `Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` (or `nextRound(onDiskBefore) - 1` for a retry) for every path, not only `args.fresh`. Impact is policy/spend and loss of the carry-forward recall aid, not memory safety — but an override that is neither advertised nor noticed defeats a gate this PR added.

samples.summary: `branchKey` keys the review round store (and thus the carry-forward text fed into the next round's verifier prompt) on process environment variables, which are attacker-chosen for a fork PR head ref
samples.evidence: `branchKey` falls back to `env.GITHUB_HEAD_REF` then `env.GITHUB_REF_NAME` (line 758) and that value becomes `reviewBase(branch)` — the directory `priorFindingsFor` later reads `verdict.json` out of and writes into `prior-findings.json`, which `panelArgs` hands to the panel as `--prior-findings` (lines 1026-1066). The docblock itself names the harm: sharing a key means sharing "one carry-forward store — `priorFindingsFor` would read another change's verdicts and put their text into this round's verifier prompt." The delta reduces the blast radius (previously every detached checkout shared the literal `HEAD` slot) but makes the key depend on untrusted-ish input: (a) `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is the PR head ref NAME, chosen by the PR author, so on a persistent/self-hosted runner two PRs that pick the same branch name land in the same base and one can seed model-written `verdict.json` text that the other carries into its verifier prompt; (b) any parent process/shell profile that exports `GITHUB_REF_NAME` makes a local detached-HEAD run adopt an arbitrary attacker-nameable key; (c) the `detached-unknown` terminal fallback (line 763) is a single shared slot for every keyless detached run on the machine, re-creating exactly the mixing the function exists to prevent. Cross-USER planting is blocked by the 0700/uid leaf guard in `unsafeBaseReason`, which is why confidence is low and I could not complete an end-to-end exploit; the same-uid / same-runner cases above still deliver another review's text into a prompt held by a session with repo write access. Preferring the git-observable commit (`detached-<sha>`) over the env, or mixing the sha into the hash even when an env ref is used, removes the environment from the trust boundary. Note also that `branch` is interpolated raw into the log at line 1052 without `printable()`, unlike every other externally-sourced string this file prints.

samples.summary: `mkdirSync(requested)` runs before any ancestor validation, so a hostile symlinked ancestor gets a directory created inside it before the (now correct) refusal fires
samples.evidence: Lines 903-910 create the leaf, and only afterwards does the code lstat the leaf (916) and walk the resolved ancestor chain (938-945). With `--out /tmp/link/dir` where `/tmp/link` is a foreign-owned symlink, `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` materialises `dir` inside the attacker's target before line 945 refuses the run under the new `!leaf` ownership rule. No data is written there (every `readdirSync`/`writeFileSync` below now uses the resolved, validated `base`), so this is residue and a run-happened signal rather than an exposure — the delta's ownership rule is what closes the dangerous half. Validating the realpath of `path.dirname(requested)` before creating anything would leave nothing behind.

samples.summary: `unsafeBaseReason` fails OPEN when `stat.mode` is not a number, directly under the new ancestor ownership rule the delta added
samples.evidence: Line 548: `if (typeof stat.mode !== "number") return "";` — a stat object with a missing/odd `mode` is accepted as safe, whereas every other unknown on this path (`!stat`, unreadable, un-lstat-able) is refused with a reason. Real `fs.Stats` from `lstatSync` always carries a numeric mode on both POSIX and Windows, so I could not construct a live vector; it is a pre-existing line, but the delta adds a new ownership branch immediately above it and inherits the same fail direction. Returning "it could not be inspected" there would keep the function fail-closed as its docblock claims ("Fails closed: an unreadable or un-stattable base is refused too").

verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (branchKey env fallbacks at spec-to-pr.mjs:755-764, reviewBase:771-775, priorFindingsFor:839-849 feeding panelArgs --prior-findings at 1026-1066), but the claimed attack chain does not hold in this repository. (a) The fork-PR/persistent-runner premise has no instance: spec-to-pr.mjs is a local dev front door (header lines 1-31), no workflow in .github/ invokes it (grep: zero matches), and every runner is ubuntu-latest with an ephemeral tmpdir, so GITHUB_HEAD_REF/GITHUB_REF_NAME are never set where this runs; locally a non-detached checkout returns at line 757 without consulting env. (b) The env is not the enabler: reviewBase (771-775) derives the path deterministically from a PUBLIC branch name (sanitize + sha1 suffix), so any actor who can seed another review's slot must already hold same-uid write access to <tmp>/wafflebase-self-review/ and could equally plant under the git-observable detached-<sha> or a literal branch key — the proposed fix removes no capability. Cross-user planting, the only real trust boundary, is refused by unsafeBaseReason (522-570) applied to the leaf and every resolved ancestor at 914-945. (c) The detached-unknown slot (763) is unreachable from the CLI: it needs sha === "" (871-874), which only occurs with no HEAD commit, and in that state the abbrev-ref call at 875 also throws, returning fail() at 877. (d) No injection/traversal is possible from the env-derived name: line 772 strips all characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-], truncates to 60, and always appends -<hash>. The residual raw interpolation of branch at line 1052 is at most a cosmetic log-escape nit on a developer-owned string, not a blocking security defect.

finding.summary: Ancestor safety rule ignores ownership, so a foreign-owned (non-root) ancestor — including a world-writable *sticky* one — is accepted, leaving the predictable review base replaceable by that user
finding.evidence:
`unsafeBaseReason` deliberately applies the uid check only to the leaf (line 529: `if (leaf && ... stat.uid !== uid)`), and for ancestors accepts anything whose mode has no group/other write bit, plus an explicit exemption for sticky directories (line 545-551: `const forbidden = leaf ? 0o077 : 0o022; if ((stat.mode & forbidden) !== 0 && !(!leaf && (stat.mode & STICKY) !== 0))`). Two consequences on a shared machine, both reachable on the DEFAULT path `os.tmpdir()/wafflebase-self-review/<branch>-<hash>` (spec-to-pr.mjs:723-727):

(1) Sticky does not restrain the directory's OWNER. POSIX sticky only says an entry may be removed/renamed by the entry's owner, the DIRECTORY's owner, or root. An attacker (uid 1001) pre-creates `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review` mode 1777 owned by themselves — any user may set the sticky bit on their own directory. `mkdirSync(base, {recursive:true, mode:0o700})` (line 836) then creates our leaf inside it; the leaf is ours and 0700 so the leaf check passes, and the ancestor check passes because `(0o1777 & 0o022) != 0` is excused by the STICKY branch. The attacker, as owner of that sticky directory, may still rename our leaf away and put a directory or symlink of the same name in its place at any point after the check — every subsequent `writeFileSync(diffFile...)` (line 941) and every `readFileSync(.../verdict.json)` (lines 761, 783) then lands on / comes from attacker-controlled storage.

(2) Mode bits on a directory you do not own are attacker-mutable. An ancestor owned by another non-root user at 0755 passes (`0o755 & 0o022 === 0`), yet that user can `chmod 0777` at any moment and replace our directory; the guard runs once, before the panel's multi-minute run.

The file's own docblock (lines 505-509) states the impact: the review directory holds the branch diff, and `priorFindingsFor` reads `verdict.json` back into the next round's verifier prompt — "anyone who can write that path can put text into an agent session holding the developer's cre

verdict.reason: The claimed code does not exist in this tree. `unsafeBaseReason` DOES apply an ownership rule to ancestors: scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:545-547 returns "it is owned by uid N, neither root nor <uid>" for any non-leaf whose uid is neither ours nor 0, and it returns BEFORE the mode/sticky logic at 563-569. Both vectors the finding describes are therefore blocked: (1) an attacker-owned sticky 1777 `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` is refused at 545 (the sticky exemption at 565 is unreachable for a foreign owner), and (2) a third user's 0755 ancestor is likewise refused at 545, so its mutable mode bits are never relied on. The ancestor walk at 938-945 covers every resolved ancestor from dirname(base) to the root (including `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` and `<tmp>`), and a failure aborts via fail() at 944 before any diff write or verdict read. The in-code rationale at 535-544 names exactly the hazard the finding raises, and tests at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:660-673 assert `anc(0o41777, 999)` is refused while only root-owned (670) and self-owned (671) ancestors pass. The finding's quoted line numbers (529, 545-551) also do not match the quoted code here.

finding.summary: Ancestors are validated on the realpath-resolved chain while every later read/write uses the unresolved path, so an attacker-owned symlink ancestor can be re-pointed after the check (TOCTOU)
finding.evidence: Line 851-855 resolves the base (`realpathSync(base)`) and then validates only the RESOLVED ancestors; the leaf symlink check at 842-845 covers the leaf alone. All subsequent I/O uses the unresolved `base`: `rmSync(path.join(base, name))` (869), `readdirSync(base)` (868/878/755), `writeFileSync(diffFile)` (941), and the verdict reads at 761/783. Vector on the default path: an attacker creates the symlink `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review -> /tmp` (in sticky /tmp they own their own entry, so this is permitted and only they can replace it). `mkdirSync` then creates `/tmp/<branch>-<hash>` owned by us at 0700 — the leaf check passes — and the resolved ancestor chain is just `/tmp`, root-owned 1777, which the ancestor rule explicitly accepts. Once the check is done the attacker re-points the symlink at a directory of their own; the panel then writes the branch diff there and, on the next round, reads `verdict.json` from attacker-controlled content straight into the verifier prompt (the injection channel the docblock at 505-509 names). The guard never re-validates, and the panel run is minutes long. Hardening would mean opening the base once (fd / O_NOFOLLOW-style handle) or re-comparing `realpathSync(base)` immediately before each round's writes, or refusing when any UNRESOLVED ancestor component is a symlink not owned by us or root.

verdict.reason: The finding claims ancestors are validated on the realpath-resolved chain while "every later read/write uses the unresolved path". In the working tree that is not the code. scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:934-937 assigns `base = realpathSync(requested)` and every subsequent filesystem operation uses the RESOLVED `base`: roundsOnDisk(base) (949), readdirSync(base)/rmSync(path.join(base,name)) (955-956), `dir = path.join(base, round-N)` (986) feeding diffFile/changedFile writes (1013-1014, 1037-1038), and priorFindingsFor(base, round) (994, 1026) which reads verdict.json via path.join(base, ...) (812, 822, 844). A grep for `requested` shows it survives only in mkdirSync (904), the unresolved leaf lstat (916) and three refusal messages (909, 919, 944) — no post-validation I/O uses it. The claimed evidence line numbers also do not match the file (842-855 are priorFindingsFor/blockingFindingsIn; 941 is the ancestor lstat; 755/761/783 are branchKey/docblock). The concrete vector is closed as well: the leaf is refused if it is a symlink (916-919, unsafeBaseReason 524), and realpathSync yields a symlink-free path, so re-pointing `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` afterwards cannot redirect any later lookup; ancestors of the resolved chain are additionally required to be root/us-owned and not foreign-writable-non-sticky (545-547, 563-569). reviewBase is referenced nowhere else in the repo (774, 888), so there is no alternate unresolved-path consumer.
